newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan jails 19 coup plotters for up to 15 years.
newsitem.headline: Sudan jails 19 coup plotters for up to 15 years.

text.p: A Sudanese military court has sentenced 19 people to jail for trying to overthrow the Islamist government of President Omar Hassan al-Bashir last year, a government newspaper said on Wednesday.

The coup leader, army Colonel Abdel Kerim al-Nagr, was originally sentenced to 20 years in prison but Bashir, as commander-in-chief of the army, reduced this to 15 years, the newspaper al-Anbaa added.
The other 18 received sentences ranging from one month to five years. The newspaper said the trial lasted seven months but did not say when the court passed sentence.
Nine other defendants, including three officers and a retired general, were acquitted, the paper added.

Last October Defence Minister Hassan Abdel-Rahman Ali told parliament the conspirators planned to attack vital installations in Port Sudan on the Red Sea with Eritrean help and to overthrow the government.
Eritrea supports opposition groups fighting the Khartoum government, which it says is destabilising the region.
The Sudanese opposition Democratic Unionist Party said the Sudanese authorities fabricated the conspiracy story to cover up a purge of army officers hostile to Bashir.

In February the New York-based group Human Rights Watch said the procedures in the secret military trial made a mockery of justice. The defendants had no right to lawyers and the court was not legally qualified, it added.
